title: Revolutionizing Expense Management: How GCS Streamlined T&E Reporting with ERP Integration
content:
In today’s fast-paced business environment, operational efficiency can make or break a company’s ability to scale effectively. For businesses like Global consultancy services ltd (GCS), a global accounting and consulting firm, staying on top of their financial management processes is critical to maintaining growth and profitability. One key area where GCS faced significant challenges was managing employee travel and entertainment (T&E) expenses.

With corporate credit cards issued to employees, the company was facing inefficiencies in recording each transaction in their NetSuite ERP system. The manual entry process was time-consuming, error-prone, and required considerable resources. As a result, GCS sought out solutions to streamline this process, reduce manual work, and improve accuracy—ultimately saving time and costs.

This is where Contetra stepped in, leveraging our deep expertise as ERP functional consultants to implement a tailored solution that simplified GCS’s T&E expense reporting process, integrated seamlessly with their existing system, and ultimately saved them around 20 man-hours per month.

The Challenge: Cumbersome Expense Reporting

For many businesses, managing employee expenses is no small task. When companies issue corporate credit cards to employees, recording each purchase and ensuring it aligns with company policy is critical—but also time-consuming.

For GCS, the situation was no different. Employees were regularly making business-related purchases using corporate credit cards, but the process of recording these transactions in NetSuite was a cumbersome and inefficient one. The finance team had to manually enter each expense into the system, a process that was not only time-consuming but also prone to errors. As the business grew and more employees were issued corporate cards, the volume of transactions increased, making this manual entry even more unmanageable.

This inefficiency began to eat into valuable time and resources. The manual process made it difficult for the finance team to keep up, and tracking these transactions in real-time became a challenge. Without automated processes in place, the time spent on administrative tasks was detracting from the team’s ability to focus on more value-driven activities, such as financial analysis and decision-making.

Contetra’s Solution: Automating T&E Expense Reporting Through ERP Integration

Recognizing the need for a more efficient solution, GCS partnered with Contetra, an expert in ERP functional consulting services. As experienced ERP functional consultants, we were able to offer a solution that not only addressed the immediate challenge but also provided long-term benefits for the organization.

Our approach focused on automating the manual entry of corporate credit card transactions into NetSuite, reducing the need for time-intensive data entry and enhancing overall accuracy. The solution we proposed was a file-based integration that would allow credit card transaction data to be automatically imported into NetSuite without manual intervention. Here’s how we executed it:

  1. File-Based Integration Setup: Instead of manually entering each credit card transaction, we integrated a file-based process that automatically pulls data from the credit card providers directly into NetSuite. This integration was designed to work seamlessly with GCS’s existing workflows and allowed for automatic categorization of expenses based on predefined rules.

  2. Automated Approval Workflows: To ensure that the expense data was reviewed and approved according to company policies, we implemented automated approval workflows. Managers could review expenses and approve them in real-time, reducing bottlenecks and improving the speed of the overall process. This automated workflow reduced the manual steps involved in verifying and categorizing expenses, saving considerable time.

By automatically importing the credit card data into NetSuite, the finance team could monitor T&E expenses more closely and ensure compliance with company policies. The integration also provided improved visibility into spending patterns, helping GCS make more informed decisions on budget allocation and expense management.

The Outcome: Significant Time Savings and Increased Efficiency

The solution we implemented brought significant improvements for GCS, both in terms of operational efficiency and cost savings. Here’s a breakdown of the key outcomes:

  1. Time Savings of 20 Man-Hours Per Month: By automating the process of recording T&E expenses, GCS saved approximately 20 man-hours per month. These hours, previously spent on manual data entry and transaction reconciliation, were redirected towards more strategic tasks. As a result, the finance team was able to focus on higher-value activities, such as analyzing cash flow, preparing reports, and making data-driven financial decisions.

  2. Enhanced Accuracy and Reduced Errors: One of the key benefits of the integration was the significant reduction in errors. Manual data entry is often prone to human error, especially when handling large volumes of transactions. By automating the process, we ensured that all credit card transactions were recorded accurately, eliminating discrepancies and improving the quality of financial data.

  3. Better Financial Control: With the automated integration in place, GCS’s finance team had greater control over the company’s expense management. They could easily track all T&E expenses in real-time, ensuring that all transactions adhered to company policies. The improved visibility also helped the finance team make better financial decisions, optimizing their budgeting process and helping identify potential areas for cost savings.

  4. Scalability: As GCS continues to grow, the system we implemented was designed to scale with the company. The integration can handle increased transaction volumes without the need for additional manual work. This means that as GCS adds more employees or issues more corporate cards, the process remains efficient and manageable.

The Bigger Picture: ERP Integration as a Key to Business Efficiency

GCS’s experience demonstrates how integrating ERP systems with day-to-day business operations can lead to significant improvements in efficiency and accuracy. At Contetra, we understand that businesses often face challenges when it comes to scaling operations and managing growing workloads. That’s where our expertise as ERP functional consultants comes into play.

By leveraging ERP systems like NetSuite, companies can save time, reduce costs, and make more informed decisions, all while focusing on growth and innovation.

Whether you’re looking to automate financial reporting, integrate new systems, or scale your business processes, we provide end-to-end ERP consulting services to help your business succeed.

Final Thoughts: A Path to Smarter Business Management

The partnership between GCS and Contetra highlights the power of ERP systems in transforming business operations. By automating manual processes and integrating key systems, GCS was able to streamline T&E expense reporting, save time, reduce errors, and gain better financial control.

If you’re facing similar challenges, consider how an ERP solution can streamline your operations and make your business more efficient. At Contetra, we’re here to help you every step of the way, from implementation to optimization, so you can focus on what matters most: growing your business.

The combined effect of lower financial costs, better resource allocation, and a more strategic approach to new product development gave the company the competitive edge it needed to grow.

The Role of Strategic Financial Management

title: Finding Financial Talent: Why Is It So Hard, and What Can You Do About It?
content:
Let’s be honest: hiring for finance roles isn’t exactly a walk in the park. It’s like hunting for that last slice of pizza at a party—you know it’s out there, but so does everyone else, and they’re faster. Finance recruitment 2025 is more competitive than ever, with a high demand for skilled professionals and a limited talent pool.

But don’t sweat it. Finding the right talent doesn’t have to be an endless struggle. The truth is, there are ways to make it easier (and no, they don’t involve selling your soul). Let’s unpack why financial recruitment feels like solving a Rubik’s Cube blindfolded and what you can do to simplify the process.

Why Is Finance Hiring So Tricky?

First of all, let’s give the financial world some credit—it’s hard. This isn’t about finding someone who just punches numbers into a calculator all day (though hey, shoutout to calculators for their service). The expectations are high, and here’s why:

  1. Everybody Wants the Best

The thing about great finance professionals? They’re rare. And when they’re out there, every company wants them. It’s like trying to hire the MVP in a fantasy football league—you’re not the only one drafting. That’s why working with a finance recruitment consultant can help you tap into hidden talent pools before your competitors do.

  1. The Rulebook Is Always Changing

Finance is packed with rules, regulations, and new compliance laws that pop up faster than the latest TikTok trend. You need someone who not only knows today’s rules but can roll with the punches when tomorrow’s change.

  1. It’s Not Just Numbers, It’s People Skills

Let’s face it: financial experts who can rock spreadsheets, manage risks, and explain it all in plain English to non-finance people? That’s a unicorn. And unicorns, as we know, are not exactly hanging out on LinkedIn.

  1. No Room for Error

A bad hire in finance doesn’t just mean wasted time—it can mean actual financial loss, compliance fines, or reputational damage. That’s why many businesses are turning to outsourcing finance recruitment to ensure they get the right person the first time.

OK, So What’s the Plan?

Finding great talent doesn’t have to be as painful as it sounds. Sure, it takes effort, but with a smart approach, you can make the process way less stressful. Here are a few tips:

  1. Be Crystal Clear on What You Need

Before you even think about hiring, sit down and figure out exactly what you’re looking for. What skills are non-negotiable? What’s the ideal mix of experience, qualifications, and soft skills? The clearer your job description, the more likely you are to attract the right people.

  1. Stop Fishing in the Same Pond

A lot of companies fall into the trap of looking in the same places for candidates. Broaden your horizons! Consider passive candidates (people who aren’t actively applying but might be open to the right opportunity), tap into your professional network, or explore niche job boards that specialize in finance roles. A finance recruitment consultant can also help you identify and reach out to high-potential candidates that you might otherwise miss.

  1. Don’t Overlook Cultural Fit

Sure, technical skills matter, but so does how someone fits into your team. A brilliant finance director who can’t work collaboratively or adapt to your company’s culture is going to cause more headaches than they solve.

  1. Streamline Your Process

Long, drawn-out recruitment processes are a recipe for disaster. Good candidates won’t wait around forever—they’ll move on to other opportunities. Make your hiring process efficient: no unnecessary steps, no ghosting, and keep communication clear and timely.

The Not-So-Secret Weapon: Outsourcing

Look, sometimes you’ve just got too much on your plate. You’ve got budgets to review, stakeholders to impress, and probably a hundred unread emails. Adding “find the perfect finance hire” to your to-do list can feel like overkill. That’s where outsourcing finance recruitment comes in handy.

Finance recruitment 2025 is evolving rapidly, and top finance recruitment agencies in India have access to a global network of professionals. They’ve got the expertise, industry connections, and technology to find candidates that fit both your skill requirements and company culture.

Sure, you could do it all yourself—but if someone’s offering to make your life easier, why not?

Why It’s Worth Putting in the Effort

Here’s the thing about hiring the right finance talent: when you get it right, it’s a total game-changer. A great hire isn’t just someone who can crunch numbers—it’s someone who can help your business grow, adapt to change, and make smarter decisions.

The right person will bring fresh ideas to the table, streamline your processes, and give you the confidence to tackle whatever challenges come your way. And honestly? It’s worth taking the time to find them.

Finance recruitment 2025 is tough. The talent pool is competitive, the stakes are high, and nobody wants to make a bad hire. But with a clear plan, some smart strategies, and maybe a little help from the pros, you can find the perfect person for the job.

So next time you’re staring down a pile of resumes and wondering where all the unicorns are hiding, just remember: the right talent is out there. It might take a little patience and a little creativity to find them, but when you do? Totally worth it.

title: Offshore Accounting for Cloud-Based Software Companies: Streamlining Subsidiary Reporting and Unlocking Operational Efficiency
content:
Cloud-based software companies operate in a fast-moving industry where agility, precision, and scalability are essential. With expansion often comes the establishment of multiple subsidiaries across the globe, each navigating its own regional regulations, currencies, and compliance frameworks. But while global growth is exciting, it can turn into an accounting nightmare if not handled properly.

Enter offshore accounting. For cloud-based software companies, outsourcing key financial tasks to offshore accounting and taxation services has proven to be more than just a cost-cutting move—it’s a strategic approach to achieving operational excellence.

One of the most significant wins in offshore accounting services is the ability to streamline reporting periods across multiple subsidiaries, ensuring timely, accurate, and uniform financial insights. But how does it work, and why is it so important? Let’s dive in.

The Challenge of Reporting Periods Across Subsidiaries

For companies with subsidiaries in different regions, synchronizing financial reporting periods can feel like solving a Rubik’s Cube in the dark. Each subsidiary may follow its own accounting calendar, driven by local regulations or legacy systems. The result?

  • Delayed Consolidation: Parent companies often have to wait weeks—or even months—for reports from subsidiaries, making it difficult to get a clear financial picture.

  • Mismatched Data: Different reporting periods create discrepancies that require significant manual effort to reconcile.

  • Missed Opportunities: With delayed reporting, decision-makers are forced to operate on outdated data, making it harder to respond quickly to market changes or investment opportunities.

For one of our clients—a growing SaaS company with six subsidiaries spanning the US, Europe, and Asia—this issue was particularly problematic. Each subsidiary had a different reporting cycle, which meant the parent company’s consolidated reports were often weeks behind schedule. The finance team spent countless hours reconciling mismatched data, leaving little time for strategic analysis.

How Offshore Accounting Solves This

When this SaaS company approached us at Contetra, their objective was simple: bring all subsidiaries into a synchronized reporting cycle without disrupting day-to-day operations. Here’s how we made it happen:

  1. Unified Reporting Calendar

We started by creating a single, standardized reporting calendar for all subsidiaries. This calendar aligned with the parent company’s reporting deadlines while respecting regional compliance requirements.

  1. Centralized Offshore Team

Our offshore accounting team acted as a hub, managing reporting for all six subsidiaries. Instead of relying on each subsidiary’s local team to prepare reports, we centralized the process, ensuring consistency and accuracy.

  1. Automation Tools

We implemented bookkeeping services automation tools to speed up data collection and eliminate errors. By integrating the company’s ERP system with offshore accounting services, we ensured that all subsidiaries fed real-time data into a centralized dashboard. This eliminated the need for manual data consolidation.

The Results:

  • Reporting delays were reduced from three weeks to just five days.

  • Consolidation errors dropped by 85%, thanks to standardized processes and automation.

  • The finance team saved over 40 hours per month, which they redirected toward strategic initiatives like budgeting and forecasting.

Why Reporting Period Streamlining Matters

Streamlining reporting periods isn’t just about making life easier for the accounting team—it has a tangible impact on business outcomes. Here’s why it’s a game-changer for cloud-based software companies:

  • Faster Decision-Making: Timely, consolidated reports give leadership real-time insights into the company’s financial health, enabling faster, data-driven decisions.

  • Improved Cash Flow Management: Synchronizing reporting cycles provides a clearer picture of cash flow across subsidiaries, helping companies plan expenditures and investments more effectively.

  • Investor Confidence: For SaaS companies seeking funding or preparing for an IPO, streamlined reporting demonstrates financial discipline and transparency, which are key to attracting investors.

Tackling Complexities: A Real-Life Example

One SaaS client faced an additional layer of complexity: some subsidiaries reported in different currencies, while others followed varying tax reporting requirements. On top of synchronizing reporting periods, they needed a system that could handle:

  • Currency conversions in real time.

  • Adherence to local GAAP or IFRS, depending on the region.

  • Integration with subscription revenue data, a key component of their financial model.

Our offshore team built a customized solution:

  • A centralized currency conversion tool automated real-time exchange rate updates.

  • Region-specific compliance modules ensured local tax laws were accounted for while still aligning with the parent company’s consolidated framework.

  • Revenue data from subscription management tools like Stripe was seamlessly integrated into the accounting system, providing accurate monthly recurring revenue (MRR) insights.

The outcome? A 30% faster month-end close process and a leadership team that finally had reliable, up-to-date financial reports at their fingertips.

Offshore Accounting: Beyond Reporting

While streamlining reporting periods is a standout benefit, offshore accounting services brings much more to the table for cloud-based software companies.

  1. Cost Efficiency

Let’s not beat around the bush—hiring in-house accountants in high-cost regions can strain your budget. Offshore accounting teams offer the same level of expertise (or better) at a fraction of the cost, freeing up resources for other priorities like R&D or customer acquisition.

  1. Scalability

Growing fast? Offshore accounting teams can scale alongside you. Whether you’re adding new subsidiaries or navigating tax season, they provide the flexibility to adjust support levels as needed.

  1. Focus on Core Competencies

By outsourcing routine tasks like reconciliations, payroll, and tax compliance, your internal team can focus on strategic initiatives that drive growth.

Final Thoughts

title: Strategic Business and Financial Management: How FlexoPress Turned Around Its Growth Trajectory
content:
In the highly competitive world of industrial manufacturing, businesses must constantly evolve their financial and strategic approach to stay profitable and sustainable. FlexoPress, a leading manufacturer of Flexo printing presses, plate-making machines, and solvent recovery systems, faced significant challenges in debt dependency, low sales conversion, and inefficient financial cycles. However, through a series of strategic shifts and with the assistance of fractional CFO services, the company successfully transformed its business model, improving profitability, financial efficiency, and team performance.

This transformation offers valuable insights for business owners looking to optimize their financial and operational strategies, especially those in manufacturing and capital-intensive industries. Here’s how FlexoPress navigated its challenges and turned its financials around within a year.

The Challenge: High Debt Dependency and Low Sales Conversion

Before implementing key strategic changes, FlexoPress struggled with a high dependency on debt and low sales conversion rates. Like many manufacturing businesses, working capital constraints meant they relied heavily on borrowed funds. However, without a strong cash flow strategy, debt utilization became a burden rather than a growth enabler.

Additionally, their sales structure was geographically divided, which led to inefficiencies in targeting the right customers. Instead of focusing on product-driven sales strategies, the team was structured based on regional markets, limiting their ability to cater to specific customer needs.

The Strategy: Financial and Sales Overhaul

To address these pain points, FlexoPress made three crucial strategic changes with the guidance of fractional CFO services:

  1. Shift in Customer Advance Policy
    One of the major changes was revising the customer advance policy to secure more upfront payments. This move significantly improved cash flow, reducing the need to depend on short-term loans. By asking for higher advances, FlexoPress was able to fund operations without stretching its balance sheet.

  2. Sales Team Restructuring: From Geography-Based to Product-Based
    Previously, the sales team operated based on geographical regions, which limited their specialization. Recognizing the need for a more focused approach, the company restructured the team to be product-wise instead of location-based.

This shift meant that sales personnel became product experts, understanding the technical specifications, unique value propositions, and target customer profiles of each offering. As a result, conversion rates improved, and sales efforts became more strategic rather than generalized.

  1. New Sales Incentive Policy
    Understanding that sales performance is directly tied to motivation, FlexoPress introduced a revised incentive structure to drive results. The new incentive scheme aligned rewards with revenue growth, customer acquisition, and timely collections, ensuring that sales teams were motivated to close deals effectively and quickly.

The Impact: A Financial and Operational Turnaround

The impact of these changes was both quantifiable and transformative. Within a year, FlexoPress witnessed dramatic improvements across key financial and operational metrics:

  • Debt Utilization Dropped from ₹2.5 Cr to ₹0.4 Cr

    • With better cash flow management, reliance on debt reduced significantly, improving financial health.

  • DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) Reduced from 75 Days to 30 Days

    • The improved advance payment structure and focused sales efforts led to faster receivables, improving liquidity.

  • Revenue Growth from ₹11 Cr in FY 22-23 to ₹17 Cr in FY 23-24

    • This represents a 54% increase in revenue, driven by improved sales structuring and targeted efforts.

  • Profitability Turnaround: From an 8% Loss to a 10% Profit Before Tax (PBT)

    • Better financial planning, reduced debt burden, and increased revenue led to a remarkable profit turnaround.

Beyond Numbers: Operational and Cultural Shifts

  1. While financial metrics highlight success, equally important were the operational and cultural shifts within FlexoPress:

    • Clearer Division of Roles and Responsibilities: With the restructuring of the sales team, internal clarity improved, reducing inefficiencies and role overlaps.

    • Higher Employee Motivation: The revised incentive structure ensured that teams were driven by performance and growth, leading to a proactive approach in customer interactions.

    • Adoption of a Product-Wise Growth Approach: Instead of treating sales as a broad function, each product category was given a distinct target market and pricing strategy, making the company more agile in responding to market needs.

Key Takeaways for Business Owners

For manufacturing businesses and other capital-intensive industries, FlexoPress’s turnaround holds valuable lessons:

  1. Financial Discipline is Key: Ensuring sustainable cash flow and reducing debt reliance should be a priority.

  2. Restructuring Can Unlock Efficiency: Moving from a geographic to a product-based sales model helped streamline operations and improve conversions.

  3. Incentives Drive Results: A well-structured incentive plan can significantly boost team performance and overall revenue growth.

  4. Customer Advances Strengthen Liquidity: Having a strong advance policy improves cash cycles and reduces dependency on external funding.

The Role of Strategic Business and Financial Management

At Contetra, we help businesses like FlexoPress optimize their financial strategies, improve cash flows, and restructure operations for sustainable growth by providing virtual CFO services. Whether it’s designing better incentive plans, restructuring sales teams, or reducing financial risk, strategic business and financial management can make a tangible difference.

title: Unlock the Secrets to Mastering ERP Costs- A CFO’s Guide to Staying on Budget.
content:
Is your ERP system draining your budget more than it should? If so, you’re not alone.

For many CFOs, IT managers, and business leaders, managing ERP-related expenses is a constant challenge. ERP implementations often start with good intentions but end up over budget and under-delivering. Costs creep in from unexpected places — customizations, training, maintenance — and without a strategic approach, these projects can become financial black holes. That’s why working with an experienced ERP functional consultant from the beginning can make all the difference.

But here’s the good news: it doesn’t have to be this way.                                                                                                                                                                            

With the right strategies in place, you can turn your ERP system into a cost-efficient powerhouse that not only supports your business operations but also delivers measurable value. If you’re ready to regain control, it’s time to unlock six proven strategies that will keep your ERP costs in check and help your business stay on track.

1. Plan and Budget with Precision

The foundation of cost-effective ERP implementation is detailed planning and budgeting. Too often, businesses jump into ERP projects with a vague estimate or high-level roadmap, only to be blindsided by unanticipated expenses later.

Start by reviewing your past ERP expenditures to understand where your money has gone. Identify recurring costs, inefficiencies, and areas that delivered the most value. From there, prioritize spending on the elements that directly support your strategic goals. For example, system upgrades that enhance core functionality often offer a better return on investment than non-essential features.

Next, forecast your future needs. Consider your company’s growth trajectory, upcoming technology trends, and internal resource capabilities. Regularly monitor and adjust your budget throughout the year to stay aligned with real-time changes.

Even a simple budget template can be a game changer. Allocate clear cost estimates to key categories like software licenses, data migration, training, and support. A little preparation now can save you a lot of money and frustration later.

2. Customize with Purpose, Not Excess

ERP customization is one of the most common budget pitfalls. While it’s tempting to tailor every function to your specific business needs, excessive customization can be both expensive and unsustainable.

Take the example of Malabar Gold and Diamonds. They were struggling with disconnected systems across their supply chain. Instead of investing in extensive customization, they implemented Microsoft Dynamics 365 using industry-specific templates. This decision helped them avoid more than $1 million in unnecessary customization costs.

The lesson here is clear: customize where it counts but avoid overengineering your solution. Focus on what adds genuine value and look for smart workarounds like reporting tools such as Power BI that enhance functionality without inflating the budget. An experienced ERP functional consultant can guide you on how to balance customisation for maximum ROI.

3. Choose the Right ERP System from the Start

Selecting the right ERP system can be the difference between long-term success and ongoing frustration. It’s not just about features; it’s about fit.

When evaluating ERP platforms, consider your current business requirements and future scalability. Look for systems that integrate easily with your existing tools and processes and pay close attention to the total cost of ownership — not just the upfront licensing fees. User experience also matters more than you might think. A user-friendly interface leads to higher adoption rates and fewer training costs.

An ERP selection consultant can provide invaluable support during this stage. By leveraging their expertise, you reduce the risk of needing costly changes or full reimplementation later.

4. Maximize ROI Through Strategic Utilization

An ERP system is not a set-it-and-forget-it solution. Its true value is unlocked through consistent utilization, proper training, and the ability to make data-driven decisions.

Ensure that your team receives the right training to use the system effectively. Encourage ongoing learning and support to foster adoption across departments. Leverage ERP data to gain insights into operations, customer behavior, and financial trends. This helps in making informed decisions that drive efficiency and profitability.

Here’s another tip: according to IFRS accounting standards, you can capitalize one-time ERP implementation costs on your balance sheet and amortize them over several years. This can significantly improve your financial management and cash flow.

5. Partner with the Right Functional Experts

Behind every successful ERP implementation is a reliable functional partner. This isn’t just someone who knows the software — it’s someone who understands your business inside and out.

A trusted ERP functional consultant helps translate your business processes into ERP configurations that work. They ensure proper system setup, test extensively before go-live, and provide training and post-launch support. They also help coordinate between technical teams, internal stakeholders, and vendors, reducing the risk of miscommunication and project delays.

In one notable case, a leading insurance broker brought in a functional partner to manage their SAP BI implementation. By clearly defining responsibilities and timelines, they were able to execute a seamless rollout with minimal disruptions.

6. Conduct Regular ERP System Audits

Once your ERP system is up and running, it’s tempting to consider the job done. But ongoing system audits are essential for identifying inefficiencies, reducing waste, and uncovering cost-saving opportunities.

Audits help ensure that your ERP is performing as expected, that processes are optimized, and that features are being fully utilized. For example, Hershey’s faced rising costs and inefficiencies after rolling out a new ERP. Regular system audits helped them detect issues early, reduce downtimes, and ultimately improve operational performance.

Periodic evaluations allow you to course-correct, reallocate resources, and continuously improve how your system supports business goals. The right ERP selection consultant can help structure these audits effectively.

Final Thoughts: ERP Doesn’t Have to Break the Bank

ERP implementations are known for being costly and complex, but with a clear strategy and expert guidance, you can manage them efficiently. By focusing on detailed planning, smart customization, thoughtful system selection, and ongoing optimization, your ERP can become a powerful driver of value — not a drain on your resources.

Whether you’re planning a new ERP rollout or trying to rein in costs from an existing system, these strategies will help you take control and build a more sustainable path forward.

Looking for hands-on guidance? At Contetra, we specialize in helping businesses master ERP costs and drive long-term success. Reach out to us today and start turning your ERP system into a strategic advantage — with the support of experienced and trusted ERP selection consultants.

title: How Apex Vitals Found Pricing Clarity with Contetra's Strategic Costing Tools
content:
Fractional CFO Services are becoming a game-changer for growing businesses seeking financial clarity without hiring a full-time executive. In today’s volatile market, where price sensitivity and competition dominate every sector, precision in pricing is not just a strategic advantage it’s a necessity. For import-driven businesses, where multiple variables impact landed cost, pricing missteps can quickly erode profit margins and jeopardize sustainability.

Apex Vitals, a healthcare product import company, was experiencing this firsthand. While the company had successfully scaled its operations, it struggled with a fundamental financial roadblock: accurately determining the cost of imported products and setting optimal, break-even-oriented selling prices.

Here’s how Contetra helped them turn that challenge into a repeatable, strategic capability with tools that now drive their pricing and profitability decisions.

The Challenge: Pricing in the Dark

Apex Vitals was facing two major challenges:

  1. No Clear View of Landed Costs

    Imported goods are subject to a web of cost factors shipping, freight, insurance, customs, forex fluctuation, port handling, warehousing, and local delivery. Despite having a solid procurement team, Apex Vitals lacked a unified framework to account for and track these costs comprehensively. The result? Guesswork.

    Each SKU came with uncertainty. Quoting prices became a gamble, often leading to either underpricing (and margin erosion) or overpricing (and lost deals).

  2. No Structured Pricing Strategy

    While Apex had an energetic sales team, they lacked clarity on what constituted a profitable price. Without insights into gross margins, break-even points, or how incentive structures affected profitability, pricing decisions were disconnected from financial strategy.

    The company knew it needed structure. What they needed was a solution that integrated finance, pricing, and performance all in one place.

Contetra’s Solution: Clarity through Templates

Contetra stepped in with a simple but powerful philosophy: financial clarity through structure and strategy. As part of our fractional CFO services, our focus was to build easy-to-use templates that would empower the Apex Vitals team not overwhelmed them with complexity. 

  1. Cost Walkthrough Template: Know the Real Cost


We started by building a custom Excel-based walkthrough template to capture: 

  • Purchase price of goods 

  • International freight and insurance charges 

  • Customs duties, taxes, and import levies 

  • Forex adjustments (conversion rates, remittance charges) 

  • Domestic handling and delivery costs 


Every line item was mapped from the vendor invoice to warehouse shelf, enabling the finance team to view a true landed cost per unit broken down by SKU. 

What made the template effective was its automation: 

  • Preloaded formulas to avoid errors 

  • Dropdown selections to reduce manual input 

  • Built-in logic to flag inconsistencies 

Outcome: With the full support of our fractional CFO service team, Apex Vitals no longer need to rely on back-of-the-envelope calculations. Costing became accurate, repeatable, and scalable. 

  1. Selling Price & Incentive Strategy Template: Sell for Profit, Not Just Revenue


With costing under control, we turned to pricing. The goal was simple: ensure the sales team could quote prices that met break-even goals while rewarding performance. 

The pricing template allowed the team to: 

  • Input expected gross margins 

  • Factor in incentives and commission payouts 

  • Determine the minimum selling price for break-even 

  • Simulate different pricing and profit scenarios 

  • Understand how incentive changes affect PAT (Profit After Tax) 


Sales leaders could now adjust margins, create incentive slabs, and see instant impact on net profitability before finalizing prices. 

Outcome: Sales and finance started working from the same playbook. Pricing became data-driven. Incentives aligned with performance. 

Business Impact: Pricing Confidence, Profit Control

Deploying these tools created immediate wins across the organization: 

✅ Accurate Product Costing 

With cost templates in place, Apex eliminated pricing errors caused by hidden or missed cost elements. Budgeting and procurement planning improved. 

✅ Strategic Pricing 

No more “gut feel” pricing. Sales teams now quoted confidently, knowing where margins stood and what price protected profitability. 

✅ Aligned Sales and Finance 

Finance and sales often speak different languages. The templates created a shared understanding – breaking silos and improving collaboration. 

✅ Data-Driven Decision-Making 

With forecasting and simulation built in, the leadership team could plan strategically instead of reacting to surprises. 

Why This Story Matters

Apex Vitals is not alone. Many businesses struggle with pricing not because of poor intentions, but because of poor systems. Without the right tools, pricing becomes reactive, margin leakage becomes common, and scaling turns into a risky game. 

What Contetra’s CFO advisory services proved was that even a simple template built with the right logic and integrated into daily workflows can transform a company’s financial clarity and decision-making. 

Strategic finance doesn’t always need a complex ERP or expensive tools. It needs structure, repeatability, and user-friendly design. That’s what we brought to Apex Vitals  and it worked. 

Final Thoughts: Pricing Is a Process, Not a One-Time Task

Most companies think of pricing as a one-off number. At Contetra, through our CFO advisory services, we help businesses understand pricing as a system one that connects cost, strategy, and execution. 

If your business: 

  • Imports goods 

  • Has sales incentives tied to performance 

  • Operates in price-sensitive markets 

  • Wants to scale sustainably 


Then it’s time to stop pricing reactively. Just like Apex Vitals, you can build clarity into your operations with tools that guide your decisions, protect your margins, and drive your growth. 

Want to know more about how we do this? Let’s talk. Together, we’ll make your finance team a strategic engine not just a back-office function.

title: 8 Actionable Strategies to Improve Your Profit After Tax (PAT) Part 1
content:
In today’s fast-evolving business landscape, success is no longer just about growing your revenue. Real business strength lies in how much of that revenue you keep after all the costs, taxes, and inefficiencies are accounted for. That’s your Profit After Tax (PAT) a true measure of how lean, smart, and sustainable your business really is.

At Contetra, we’ve worked with dozens of businesses startups, family-run companies, and funded growth-stage firms. And we’ve seen one pattern repeatedly: Businesses that focus early on strategic profitability, not just top-line growth, build resilience and attract investor confidence.

This blog is Part 1 of a two-part series where we outline eight field-tested strategies used by high-performing finance teams to increase PAT. These aren’t complex theories they’re actionable ideas that you can start implementing this quarter.

Let’s dive into the first four.

1. Move from Cost-Based to Value-Based Pricing

Traditional pricing methods rely on this formula: cost + margin = price. While it covers your expenses, it ignores your customer’s perception of value. This is where value-based pricing stands out.

Value-based pricing aligns your prices with the perceived value of your product or service, not just the cost of production. This allows you to charge higher where the customer sees real benefits speed, service, branding, reliability, or outcomes.

Take inspiration from brands like Apple or Zomato Gold. Customers don’t pay only for the product; they pay for experience, time saved, and status. That’s value-based pricing in action.

What You Can Do:

  • Identify the top three benefits your best customers care about.

  • Conduct competitor research to benchmark prices.

  • Interview sales teams to understand what customers actually value.

  • Package offerings in a way that highlights outcome, not effort.


Over time, this shift can increase both pricing power and customer lifetime value. An ERP functional consultant can help structure your costing and pricing models within your ERP system to reflect real-time insights that support value-based pricing decisions.

2. Build a Sales Funnel That Converts

Many companies complain about lead quality or low conversion rates. But often the real issue is the lack of a structured sales funnel.

A well-structured sales funnel gives your team a roadmap to move leads from awareness to decision, with clear checkpoints and triggers at every stage.

Structure it in three simple stages:

  • Awareness: Get in front of your audience with social media reels, Google ads, and customer referrals.

  • Consideration: Educate them. Use webinars, case studies, free resources, or toolkits that show your credibility.

  • Decision: Close with high-conversion landing pages, proof of ROI, clear CTAs, and real testimonials.


Sales funnels also let you forecast revenue more reliably and reduce your customer acquisition cost (CAC). A skilled ERP selection consultant can help align your ERP and CRM systems to track conversions, manage leads, and forecast revenue in real-time.

Quick Tip: Use a simple CRM like Zoho, Pipedrive, or even Google Sheets to track leads, automate reminders, and monitor conversion metrics.

Even a 10% increase in funnel conversion can improve your PAT significantly by making your marketing spend more efficient.

3. Keep More of What You Earn Through Smart Tax Planning

Your business might be profitable on paper, but how much of that reaches the bank depends on tax planning.

Effective tax optimization doesn’t mean bending rules. It means using incentives, schemes, and timing to your advantage.

One powerful example is presumptive taxation. If your business turnover is under ₹3 crores (and 95% of receipts are non-cash), you can opt to declare 6-8% of your receipts as income simplifying compliance and reducing the overall tax burden.

Other tax-saving levers include:

  • Strategic depreciation of assets

  • Investment-linked deductions under sections like 35AD

  • Timely expense booking and provisioning

  • TDS and advance tax management


What You Can Do:

  • Get a mid-year tax health check done by a CA.

  • Avoid last-minute tax planning in March it’s usually too late.

  • Track recurring expenses to make sure they’re recorded correctly.


Every ₹1 saved on tax goes directly to PAT. And that’s real profitability.

4. Fix Your Accounting Foundation

What gets measured gets managed. If your accounting is inconsistent, delayed, or just plain wrong  you’re flying blind.

Accounting isn’t just a compliance tool. It’s a strategic system to measure your financial health, uncover inefficiencies, and plan for the future.

To fix your foundation, start with these three essentials:

  • Accrual-based accounting: Recognize revenue when earned, not when received. This gives a truer picture of performance.

  • Expense matching: Align your costs with the revenues they helped generate.

  • Depreciation and amortization: Reflect the wear and tear of assets accurately. This also reduces taxable income in a legitimate way.


We’ve worked with companies that had excellent products but poor accounting. Once we cleaned up their books and structured their MIS, they realized they were leaking margin through untracked expenses, delayed collections, and hidden liabilities.

An ERP functional consultant can also help identify whether your current ERP system is equipped to support automated financial reporting, compliance, and data visibility.

Pro Tip: Switch from Tally to cloud-based systems like Zoho Books or QuickBooks if you need better visibility and automation.

What’s Next?

You’ve now seen how pricing, sales funnels, tax strategy, and accounting are not isolated functions they are levers that directly impact your Profit After Tax.

In Part 2, we’ll cover four more strategies:

  • How ERP systems and tech reduce inefficiencies

  • Why inventory should work like cash, not stock

  • Cutting costs without hurting customer experience

  • And how consistency, not intensity, wins in the long run


Engaging an ERP functional consultant during this transformation ensures you not only implement the right tools but also optimize them to drive maximum profitability.

Implement even two of these eight strategies, and you’ll start seeing measurable impact on your margins.

Final Thoughts

Profit After Tax is the true heartbeat of your business. It tells you if your growth is real, scalable, and worth the effort.

It’s time to stop focusing only on revenue and start getting strategic about what you keep. That’s what separates thriving businesses from those that barely survive.

If you’re ready to build a PAT-focused strategy into your business, Contetra’s team of experts from finance professionals to experienced ERP selection consultants is here to help.

Stay tuned for Part 2.

title: 8 Actionable Strategies to Improve Your Profit After Tax (PAT) Part 2
content:
Part 2: Operational Excellence, Technology, and Execution

In Part 1 of this series, we explored how value-based pricing, sales funnel optimization, tax planning, and accounting discipline can directly impact your Profit After Tax (PAT). If you haven’t read it yet, check it out first – it lays the strategic foundation.

In this second part, we move from strategy to execution.
These final four actionable tactics focus on systems, processes, and decision-making discipline. When implemented right, they transform everyday operations into lasting profit drivers.

5. Leverage Technology and ERP Systems

If your departments are working in silos, spreadsheets are your default tool, and reporting takes days not hours it’s time to modernize.
Technology isn’t a luxury. It’s the engine behind profit-centered decision-making.

Why ERP Isn’t Optional Anymore

Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems bring structure, speed, and scalability. Whether you’re a startup scaling operations or an established company trying to cut through inefficiencies, ERP systems offer:

  • Real-time visibility into sales, expenses, inventory, and receivables

  • Integrated modules for finance, HR, CRM, procurement, and manufacturing

  • Error reduction through automation and approval workflows

  • Audit-readiness and GST compliance with one-click reports

  • Data-driven decisions through instant dashboards and performance KPIs


Businesses that implement even a basic ERP report up to 30% reduction in financial reporting errors and 25-40% time savings across admin functions.

For smaller businesses, platforms like Zoho Books, QuickBooks, Tally Prime, and Marg ERP provide excellent value at low entry costs. Working with an ERP functional consultant ensures your ERP setup is tailored to your operations and finance goals.

Bonus Tip: Start with Core Finance Automation

Before investing in full-scale ERP, automate core functions like:

  • Invoice generation and tracking

  • Bank reconciliation

  • Payroll processing

  • GST and TDS compliance


Even incremental automation in these areas will immediately free up bandwidth and boost accuracy feeding directly into PAT.
An experienced ERP selection consultant can help evaluate the right platform based on your business scale, industry, and integration needs.

6. Make Inventory a Profit Center, Not a Liability

Inventory is often the biggest cash absorber in a business. Poorly managed inventory increases holding costs, leads to stock obsolescence, and strains liquidity. But with the right practices, inventory can become a working capital advantage.

Key Tactics to Optimize Inventory

  • Use Just-in-Time (JIT) procurement: Only stock what’s needed based on demand forecasts

  • Track Inventory Turnover Ratio: The faster you move stock, the less capital gets stuck

  • Forecast with precision: Use sales history, seasonality, and AI tools to anticipate demand

  • Deploy ABC Analysis: Prioritize inventory based on value and volume to manage focus


A 10% reduction in overstocking can free up lakhs in working capital annually.

The Result

  • Fewer stockouts

  • Reduced waste and spoilage

  • Better purchasing decisions

  • Stronger vendor negotiation power


Well-managed inventory reduces carrying costs and boosts cash availability directly impacting profitability. In many cases, an ERP functional consultant plays a critical role in mapping your inventory workflows into the ERP system for better planning and tracking.

7. Cut Costs Without Cutting Corners

Cutting costs doesn’t mean cutting quality. It means finding non-essential expenses and redirecting those funds to revenue-generating activities.

Areas to Start Cutting (Smartly):

  • Outsource Non-Core Functions: Move HR, IT, payroll, or legal to expert partners at a fraction of the cost

  • Renegotiate Contracts: Long-term vendor relationships often offer hidden savings review at least once a year

  • Kill Hidden Costs: Unused software subscriptions, inflated travel bills, under-utilized assets

  • Streamline Approval Workflows: Reduce delays and leakages in expense processing


Companies that actively monitor vendor contracts save up to 10-12% on procurement costs annually.

The Lean Thinking Mindset

Lean isn’t about austerity. It’s about clarity. Ask:

  • Is this cost helping me generate more revenue?

  • Can this process be done faster or cheaper without losing quality?

  • Is there a tech-based alternative to this manual task?

By treating every rupee as an investment, you drive your PAT forward even when top-line growth is stagnant.

8. Execute Relentlessly and Track Consistently

Knowing what to do is just 10% of the job. Doing it, tracking it, and refining it is the other 90%.
Consistency in execution is where high-performing companies outpace their competition.

The Execution Checklist:

  • Weekly and monthly financial reviews with actionable KPIs

  • Ownership mapping every strategy or line item should have a name next to it

  • Regular internal audits to avoid leakage in processes

  • Quarterly strategy check-ins what’s working, what’s not, what’s next

  • Celebrate small wins whether it’s 1% PAT improvement or a clean tax audit


According to Harvard Business Review, companies with structured execution tracking are 60% more likely to hit profitability goals.

Align Every Team with Profitability

Your PAT isn’t just the CFO’s concern. Every department should:

  • Know how their actions affect profitability

  • Align KPIs with business objectives

  • Have data visibility to course-correct


When teams understand how their daily work translates into PAT, motivation and ownership improve across the board.
If you’re unsure how to implement this structure, engaging an ERP selection consultant can help align team metrics within your business systems to ensure every action drives profit.

Final Word: Profitability Is a Team Sport

Over these two blogs, we’ve outlined eight high-impact strategies to boost your Profit After Tax. Let’s quickly recap:

Part 1:

  • Adopt value-based pricing

  • Build a conversion-friendly sales funnel

  • Plan tax proactively

  • Set up solid accounting practices


Part 2:

  • Use ERP to unlock efficiency

  • Turn inventory into a profit lever

  • Cut wasteful spending with clarity

  • Track and execute without fail


Each of these strategies may look small on paper. But applied consistently, they compound your margins and unlock your business’s full potential.

If you want your next quarter to outperform your last, don’t wait to overhaul everything. Start with just one of these strategies. Do it well. Track it. Then move to the next.

Because growing profit isn’t about making radical moves it’s about making the right ones, one at a time.

At Contetra, our ERP selection consultants don’t just design strategies we partner with teams to embed them into everyday workflows. That’s how our clients go from firefighting to forward-planning.

Let’s simplify your path to higher profitability one smart action at a time.

title: Top 10 Lessons from Failed ERP Implementations:What every CFO/CEO should know
content:
Thinking about implementing a new ERP system? Engaging an experienced ERP selection consultant can help you avoid common mistakes. It’s a big move – one that can supercharge your business or turn it into a headache. Believe it or not, many ERP projects end up costing way more time, money and stress than expected.

But it doesn’t have to be that way, in this short guide that we have prepared, we showcase the top 10 lessons from failed ERP implementations which will help you learn from mistakes others have made so you don’t have to!

Working with the right ERP functional consultant from the start can save both cost and implementation time.

The Kitchen Sink Syndrome

Case Study – The Cover Oregon Debacle

In 2012, Cover Oregon officials failed miserably in an attempt to establish an online healthcare marketplace. Oregon elected to simultaneously implement ‘Obamacare’ and replace all its supporting transaction processing systems. It eventually had to hire and reassign over 500 employees, spend more than $300 million, and still not process a single insurance application through the system.

Having too much on the plate sometimes places an organization in a situation where it is unprepared for the number and scale of decisions necessary. Consequently, overloaded teams wind up making one bad decision after another.

If you do not want your firm to end up like Cover Oregon, do not plan a scenario where the project gets so enormous that your team is unable to meet the deadlines.

The big lesson – Limit scope of the ERP project to the appropriate time frame.

Narrow Mindedness

Case Study – Israel Chemical Limited’s hazardous waste

In 2014, ICL’s SAP ERP implementation cost skyrocketed from $120 million to over $500 million. This massive overrun led to the cancellation of the entire implementation and also the resignation of ICL’s CEO.

The CEO handed the project over to a newcomer in the CFO’s office, who was more concerned with making sure the financial requirements were covered, without really thinking about what the manufacturing and supply chain teams needed.

Generational issues might arise when no one in the management team recognizes where the problems are.

The big lesson – Focus on all users of the ERP implementation and not just a single part of the business.

Sunny path Testing

Case Study – The National Grid Turbulence

National Grid’s ERP implementation was essentially blown away by Hurricane Sandy when the utility company aimed to integrate all of its US businesses onto a single SAP system.

Their consultants, Wipro, suggested the SAP ERP project was ready to go-live based on live test results. To their dismay the actual system did not hold up under increased workload. After the hurricane, emergency business processes were needed to fix the electric grid, which included special steps to bring in workers and materials from other utilities for the large-scale repairs. The endeavour ultimately took 2 years to clean up and cost over $585 million.

The implementation team had concentrated on “happy path” testing, which comprised evaluating functions under ideal conditions, but there had been little testing of the system in emergency situations.

The big lesson – Before launching a significant ERP project, it is critical to evaluate all of the factors that might impact preparedness.

Verifying Vendor Claims

Case Study – Waste Management’s big ball of junk

Waste Management PLC(WM) ended up in a $500 million lawsuit against SAP after it ran into some major snags when it attempted a massive SAP installation in 2005. SAP had estimated that WM could save between $106 million and $220 million with a consolidated ERP system, which they said could be up and running in just 18 months. Seeing the dollar signs, they failed to verify the SAP claims before making a decision.

WM quickly found out that there were major discrepancies between what was promised and what the software actually delivered.

The big lesson – Conducting a proof of concept may drastically decrease risks. Verify vendor claims with internal business and technical teams.

Setting Unrealistic Goals

Case Study – Nike Can’t do it

In 2000, Nike thought it could Just Do It and it kicked off a $400 million upgrade to its ERP system. To their distress, the new system resulted in $100 million of lost sales and the company also saw its share price plummet by 20% when it couldn’t fulfill orders of the highly anticipated Air Jordans.

It is essential to carefully define business and operational requirements and align them with ERP capabilities and time frames.

The big lesson – It is critical to establish realistic targets in the implementation strategy, particularly with relation to ERP functionality and project timelines.

Wrong Implementation Partners

Case Study – MillerCoors’ intoxicating scheme

In 2014, MillerCoors hired HCL to implement an ambitious plan to consolidate all its financials on a single ERP system to reduce costs and improve operational efficiency. Things quickly went south leading to MillerCoors suing HCL for $100 million. The issue arose because the planning and design phases were not adequately considered. In addition, numerous critical flaws were discovered but not resolved.

HCL’s core competence was typically viewed as implementation, rather than planning and architecture.

The big lesson – Ensure you have the right people for the job. Some firms specialize in certain stages of a project. Identify the most critical ones before hiring.

Underestimating Operational Impact

Case Study – Revlon merger deranged

Following the merger of Revlon with Elizabeth Arden Inc., The company realized it needed to bring its processes together across all its business units. The new system failed badly after going online in 2018, resulting in a $64 million revenue loss, a 6.4% stock price drop, and even a lawsuit from investors.

Revlon attempted to merge Microsoft and Oracle systems on a new SAP implementation but lacked any hands-on SAP experience. They also decided to launch without ensuring that the ERP business processes would work as planned.

Launching a system that doesn’t meet operational needs and requirements usually leads to negative effects on the business.

The Big lesson – Mind both the operational and business sides of the ERP equation.

Identify and Plan for Contingencies

Case Study – Ranpak – The cost of poor planning

The Ranpak ERP failure is a classic example of what can go wrong with a poorly planned software rollout, especially in turbulent times. The packing firm was grappling with the fallout from its new ERP system coinciding with the new year, which suffered from issues like inadequate testing and a lack of employee training, the Russia-Ukraine war added another layer of complexity.

The conflict disrupted supply chains and increased economic uncertainty, making the impact of the ERP failure even more severe.

While certain risks cannot be predicted, a solid ERP implementation plan includes some flexibility so that your losses can be minimized.

The Big Lesson – A large ERP implementation project can take time; thus it is important to not rush and plan for any delays in the rollout.

Keep all stakeholders happy

Case Study – University of Washington Skips out on fees

The University of Washington finds itself troubled after the $340 million plan to migrate to a cloud-based finance system goes downtown after the university failed to clear invoices amounting to $11 million.

The big Lesson – It is critical to consider all parties impacted by the project. This comprises not only business and functional users, but also the entire ecosystem of customers and vendors.

Do not let fees pile up

Case Study – Invacare catches a cold

Medical device manufacturer Invacare put its ERP project into a coma – but not the bills! The company’s North American unit, which was the first to move to a new system, faced a key setback in rolling out a major SAP upgrade in 2021. The company put a temporary hold on the project but still had to pay the maintenance fee every month to the system integrator. Ultimately, the fed-up board went shopping for a new CEO in August 2022.

ERP implementations are one of the most resource-intensive undertakings a business can pursue; budget and deadline mismanagement can derail or stop an ERP project entirely.

The big lesson – It is critical to accurately estimate the total cost of ownership, create a timeline that includes all services and partners, and devise a strategy to reduce cost overruns caused by change orders or delays.

The history of the complex and costly enterprise software market is filled with examples of vendor disputes, excessive hype, and epic failures.

But your story shouldn’t end this way!

From helping you pick a suitable ERP software, negotiating license costs, creating BRD and automating the process – you can rely on our expertise to implement the perfect ERP for your company! An experienced ERP functional consultant can guide you in choosing the right ERP platform that matches your business strategy.

title: Mastering the Art of AOP: Your Blueprint to Business Success
content:
The Startup struggle is real (and totally avoidable)

Imagine you’ve just started your dream business. You have got your product, killer logo, a head full of ideas, sipping countless cups of coffee and every day feels like an adventure, a never-ending roller-coaster ride. One minute you are on top of the world, and the next, you are drowning in the sea of emails, invoices and last-minute fires to put out. Exhausting, right?

Enter the hero of the day: Annual Operating Plan (AOP). Not as glamourous as a superhero with a cape but I promise you it is way more practical. Think of it as a GPS to navigate through chaotic highways of business. Without it, you will be wandering aimlessly, surviving on hope. And trust me, hope should never be your plan A. That’s where early financial planning and support through fractional CFO services can help you structure your growth with clarity.

Let’s dive into what an AOP is, why you absolutely need one, and how it can transform your business from chaotic to controlled without losing the fun!

What is an Annual Operating Plan?

In simple terms, an AOP is like a new year’s resolution for your business but way more achievable. It is a detailed roadmap of what you are going to achieve in the next 12 months and how you’re going to get there.

Imagine if your business was a car. Your AOP is your steering wheel, GPS and engine all in one. Without it, you are just a driver on a road trip without a destination you are bound to get lost!

Why Every Business needs an AOP (yes, even yours)

  • Focus: It keeps everyone on the same page, like a business group hug, ensuring your team works together towards the same targets instead of running in different directions.

  • Risk Mitigation: Spot potential roadblocks before they turn into disasters. You’ll be the superhero who sees the trouble coming in from a mile ahead.

  • Clarity: No more guessing games or aimless wandering – just clear goals and the path to achieve them.

  • Accountability: Sets targets and milestones, so you can track progress and avoid unpleasant surprises. It’s like having a scoreboard to keep everyone motivated and on their toes.

  • Resource Management: Allocates budgets wisely so you are not blowing all your cash in shiny projects. After all, it’s about making every Rupee count!

    Even startups working with limited resources can benefit by complementing their AOP with fractional CFO services to ensure disciplined execution.

The Nuts and Bolts of a Solid AOP

Creating an AOP might sound like climbing Everest in flip-flops. But its simpler than you think. Here’s a breakdown for you:

  • Set Clear Objectives: Define what you want to achieve in the next year. Be specific, measurable and realistic – No ‘I want to be billionaire overnight’ goals.

  • Forecast Sales and Revenue: Estimate how much money you want to make. Be optimistic but keep it real. You are not Jeff Bezos…yet.

  • Budget Allocation: Outline where you’ll spend your money. Marketing, salaries, R&D – Every Rupee should have a purpose.

  • Resource Planning: Identify the manpower, tools and time required for you to hit your target.

  • Risk Management: Always try to identify “what – ifs” scenarios and keep back up plans handy. Think of it as an insurance policy for your business.


Meet SnaccAttack, a quirky little start-up that sells healthy snacks with a twist – they are delicious! In the first year, SnaccAttack found its success by connecting to local farmer’s market and online but soon hit a roadblock when it came to scaling up. Sales were up one month, down the next and managing inventory proved to be a headache for the company.

Enter – Annual Operating Plan

Step 1: Setting Objective: SnaccAttack’s 12-month goal was simple: Doubling sales. But instead of dreaming about it, they wrote down every step needed to make it happen.

Step 2: Forecasting Sales: They looked at their monthly numbers and set realistic targets. No more shooting in the dark.

Step 3: Budget Allocation: Instead of blowing the money in fancy ads, they used the more budget friendly influencer marketing and better packaging – things that actually made a difference.

Step 4: Resource Planning: They hired a part-time logistics manager and invested in ERP software to track inventory, reduce waste and improve efficiency.

Step 5: Risk Management: The company identified two potential risks – Supply chain delays and customer complaints – and crafted plans to tackle them. They even created an emergency fund for any unexpected hiccups.

The Result?

With Contetra’s strategic CFO services, SnaccAttack not only doubled its revenue by the end of the year, but also expanded to new cities, built a strong customer base, and improved product quality.

Don’t Just Wing it - Plan it!

Don’t let your business run on autopilot. Whether you are a fresh startup or scaling up, your business needs an Annual Operating Plan to hit the targets you have set.

It’s time to turn those wild ambitions into actionable steps. With the right strategic CFO services, you can gain deeper financial insights, stay investor-ready, and scale with control. Get in touch with us today and take the first step toward building a structured, profitable business.

title: Why Most Finance Hires Fail And What the Right Ones Do Differently
content:
In today’s rapidly evolving business landscape, hiring the right finance talent has become more critical and more challenging than ever. The traditional approach to recruiting finance professionals often centers around resumes, certifications, and technical skills. But while these factors may check the boxes on paper, they don’t always translate into impact, adaptability, or long-term success within your business. This is something we’ve seen repeatedly at Contetra in our role as a trusted finance recruitment consultant, where hiring missteps often stem from flawed approaches, not flawed people.

At Contetra, we’ve worked with dozens of organizations that struggled with underperforming finance hires not because the individuals weren’t smart, but because the hiring process was broken. Here’s why most finance hires fail, and more importantly, what the successful ones do differently.

1. Hiring for Skill, Not Fit

Most finance leaders focus too heavily on specific technical capabilities: proficiency in Excel, knowledge of accounting standards, prior experience in audit or reporting. While these are important, they’re just the baseline.

What often gets overlooked is organizational fit: Does this person think like your business does? Are they entrepreneurial in a startup? Process-driven in a scaling enterprise? Strategic in a board-facing role? When companies hire only for skill without cultural or strategic alignment, they risk inserting a misfit into a critical function.

Fit isn’t just about personality. It’s about contextual intelligence understanding how to navigate your business model, your pace, your values. This misalignment often results in underperformance, even if the hire is technically sound.

2. Mistaking Experience for Impact

Ten years of experience in finance doesn’t automatically mean someone will thrive in your context. Many candidates have spent years in static roles without ever leading change, influencing decisions, or driving outcomes. In contrast, someone with five years of experience across fast-paced, high-responsibility environments may be far more valuable.

Experience is only meaningful when it’s linked to measurable outcomes. A resume packed with job titles is not a proxy for problem-solving ability. The right hire is someone who can connect strategy to execution and navigate complexity with confidence.

The right finance hire is not just a custodian of numbers they are a translator between data and decision-making. If your interview process doesn’t dig into outcomes, initiatives, and business impact, you’re hiring in the dark. An experienced finance recruitment consultant will help you spot this difference early.

3. Relying on Generic Job Descriptions

A job description that reads “prepare MIS reports, manage budgets, liaise with auditors” doesn’t attract transformative talent it attracts task-doers. If you want to hire finance professionals who think strategically and challenge the status quo, your job descriptions need to reflect that.

Instead, highlight challenges like “optimize the working capital cycle,” “build automated dashboards,” or “lead cost-reduction initiatives.” These signals attract finance leaders, not followers. The language of the JD is often the first impression you make on a high-caliber candidate. A smart finance recruitment consultant can help you get that language right.

4. Missing the Mindset Test

One of the biggest gaps in finance hiring is testing for mindset. Does this candidate understand your business model? Do they ask smart questions about margins, pricing, or cash flow? Are they curious about growth levers?

Great finance professionals aren’t just reactive they’re forward-thinking, analytical, and commercially aware. They don’t just report the numbers; they shape the narrative around them.

At Contetra, we often help clients build simulations and business cases into the interview process to uncover this mindset. A simple exercise like “How would you improve profitability by 5% this year?” can separate the thinkers from the processors.

Mindset is the multiplier. Technical skills are teachable critical thinking is not.

5. Underutilizing Strategic Partners

Sometimes the problem isn’t in hiring the wrong person it’s hiring too soon, or hiring for the wrong problem. We’ve seen businesses try to bring in full-time CFOs when what they really needed was interim FP&A support, systems implementation help, or cost modeling expertise.

This is where strategic partners like Contetra come in. With CFO-as-a-Service, on-demand FP&A teams, and deep ERP/tech capability, we help organizations build finance muscle without rushing to hire. This approach often leads to better outcomes, lower costs, and more strategic clarity.

We’ve seen clients bring in Contetra as a temporary solution only to realize it was the accelerator they needed. When your strategy is still evolving, a flexible finance partner may outperform even the best hire.

So What Do the Right Finance Hires Do Differently?

  • They connect numbers to business stories.

  • They ask better questions.

  • They think beyond reporting.

  • They challenge assumptions.

  • They create value, not just compliance.


And most importantly, they don’t just fit the role they shape it.

They are change agents in the truest sense moving beyond spreadsheets to strategy, from reporting to real influence.

Final Thoughts

The finance function has evolved from being a record-keeper to a strategic powerhouse. Your hiring strategy needs to evolve too.

If you want to build a finance team that drives growth, resilience, and clarity, stop hiring only for resumes and years. Start hiring for relevance, outcomes, and adaptability.

Build a team that knows how to lead with insight, not just manage information.

And when in doubt, don’t rush to hire. Talk to a strategic finance partner who can guide the function until you’re ready to build in-house.
